title: What does ConfidentialMPTMergeInbox do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of ConfidentialMPTMergeInbox and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, ConfidentialMPTMergeInbox combines incoming confidential MPT funds with the holder's spending balance. [1]

The confidential model separates an inbox from the balance used for outgoing transfers. Merging updates encrypted balance state with the required proofs rather than sending funds to another person. A visible incoming transaction therefore need not imply an immediately spendable confidential balance. Follow the reference's state transition and proof requirements before preparing the next transfer. [1]

The ConfidentialMPTMergeInbox reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using ConfidentialMPTMergeInbox, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
